profile.reading: This facility, CH2, is one of two Element Critical buildings this registry maps to 711 North Edgewood Avenue, Wood Dale, Illinois 60191, in the Chicago metro; the operator maintains separate, dedicated marketing pages for "Chicago One" and "Chicago Two," indicating these are genuinely distinct facilities the company markets separately despite sharing one mapped street address, consistent with a multi-building business park or campus rather than a single structure recorded twice. The operator's own materials associate this record with 151,000 square feet of space and 7 MW of IT capacity, alongside PCI DSS, HIPAA, and ISO 27001 compliance. Element Critical is a privately held colocation operator, rebranded from Central Colo in 2017, backed by an investor group including Mercuria, 26North, Arctos, and Safanad per Mercuria's own press materials, and describes itself as a data center infrastructure provider specializing in high-density power and advanced cooling for demanding workloads including AI and GPU infrastructure, offering colocation from individual cabinets to custom suites supporting deployments up to 50 megawatts across its current three-market portfolio (Austin, Houston, and Chicago). No founding date, year-opened figure, or further building-specific breakdown distinguishing CH1 from CH2 beyond the operator's own separate marketing pages was located in sourcing reachable this session. Wood Dale sits in DuPage County, part of the broader Chicago-area O'Hare-adjacent data center corridor that has drawn colocation and enterprise demand for its proximity to the airport, fiber density, and access to ComEd power infrastructure, alongside other operators tracked elsewhere in this registry. No independent trade-press coverage distinguishing CH2 from CH1 in construction date or expansion history was located this session.

reading.body:
Element Critical's Wood Dale facility publishes 7 MW of IT capacity across 151,000 square feet, enough to support 175 to 700 racks depending on workload density, though the operator does not disclose how power is actually distributed.

The three published certifications—PCI DSS, HIPAA, and ISO 27001—qualify the site for regulated workloads in finance and healthcare. None address the infrastructure requirements for AI training, such as high-density power delivery or low-latency interconnect between GPUs. The operator has published no technical specifications on those points, making the facility's suitability for large-scale compute difficult to assess from available data.

Among the 44 Illinois data centers this site has mapped, only 6 publish a megawatt figure. CH2's 7 MW ranks fifth within that disclosed subset and represents roughly 3 percent of Illinois's published total capacity. This modest ranking reflects either a smaller footprint than the state's largest campuses or a partial disclosure of the site's actual capability. The operator has not clarified which.
